data.headline: Principal Software Engineer at Medtronic
data.about:
Professional experience dominated by significant software architecture efforts and end-to-end software systems development.  Leading roles at a number of compelling (albeit often far too short lived) "bleeding edge" technology startups and working with a lot of great + talented people.  Some of these experiences were profitable, most of which were challenging and all were a heck of a lot of fun!

La Costa / Carlsbad

Specialties: Java, C++, SOA (Service Oriented Architectures), Web 2.0, Pervasive + Cloud Computing

The entities include the nonprofit West Health Institute and West Health Policy Center, and the for-profit West Health Investment Fund and West Health Incubator. www.westhealth.org.

Technical Lead for design & development of software + systems for Yahoo! Display Advertising Applications teams that manage all aspects of digital media advertising on Yahoo! and its partner sites.  This is one of the world's largest and most complex online advertising systems for managing display advertising campaigns across hundreds of millions of users and devices worldwide, primarily using Java + Linux + JBoss + Oracle.

Next Generation Technologies Empowering Worldwide Freedom and Democracy

Design + development of numerous new + highly secured certifiable proprietary open 64-bit JEE5/6 distributed cloud computing platforms, multi-level + multi-schema + multi-instance database infrastructures, end-to-end & electronic elections + authoring + voting + auditing + reporting systems + devices, front to back & back to front, using varied deployments of CentOS Linux + VMware + Java + JBoss + Seam + JSF + PostgreSQL + Apache, etc., & more ... to start :)

The company's truly impressive executive team included Lori Steele (one of Fortune's 2009 "Most Powerful Women in Small Business" who can reportedly see our family's house with binoculars from the backyard of her nearby Encinitas home ... her fun inside joke), Aaron Contorer (formerly Bill Gates' technical advisor and long time Microsoft + Windows / MSN / Visual Studio exec, writer of telnet + original mosaic team member & more) and Jon Thomason (also longtime MSFT + one of the founders of the Xbox group whom I remembered from back when he was Windows 95 S/W Dev. Mgr & Bill Gates hired Penn & Teller + rented Disneyland for what was then really a select few hundred early Windows developers attending the pre-Windows 95 Developer event one night up in Anaheim when I was @ Polaris) + Paul DeGregorio (former distinguished Chairman of the U.S. EAC).

Veoh was Michael Eisner's online video aggregation service using Hadoop & one of the top web sites in the US (over 28 million users per month).  The experience was much shorter than one would like but a lot of fun + challenge nonetheless (improved volume + accuracy of ingested content on the site from 27% -> 99.7%).  It was some months after that drastic change in company direction on April Fools Day 2009 before the company ultimately did later win its long sought + costly legal ruling in the landmark copyright case first brought by Universal Music Group and then a few months more before the company finally + fully collapsed, COBRA and all :(

Creating command & control + component integrations between Preventsys appliances & leading network security products including Alterpoint, Configuresoft, Foundstone, MBSA, NeXpose, NGS (Oracle + SQL Server), nCircle, Watchfire AppScan & other vendors. C++, STL, XML, XSLT, Java, SOAP.  Company ultimately acquired by McAfee.

description.text:
Graviton's gateways are distributed throughout the network to receive telesensor inputs, pre-process sensor data, and retransmit the appropriate information to the data hub via standard Web protocols or execute appropriate instructions through the telesensor module.

The MSG-1000 Multi-Services Gateway serves a bridge between one or more wireless distributed sensor networks (WDSN) and a wide area network (WAN). In a wide range of applications (such as temperature monitoring, asset monitoring, battery health assurance, energy management, and security monitoring), the MSG gateway can be used as a conduit for moving real-time analog, discrete, and video data between wireless telesensors and the secure network server, and as a distributed processor capable of performing varied application-specific functions (such as alarm detection, notification, and on-site data logging).

The MSG gateway, which runs on the Linux operating system, hosts the DIMAC MSD server software as an active component of Graviton's DIMAC architecture. The DIMAC MSG server executes distributed data acquisition and control and local alarming functions independent of the fault-tolerant DIMAC enterprise server, located at Graviton's network operations center. The enterprise server, a highly scalable platform, is designed to provide intuitive Web browser-based remote configuration tools and to transparently manage the updating of MSG's operating software.

The MSG gateway supports two wireless telesensor interfaces installed either internally on the MSG's backplane or externally and connected via serial port. The radios used in conjunction with the MSG may operate on one or more of the unlicensed ISM frequency bands-418 MHz, 900 MHz, or 2.4 GHz. Connection to a WAN can be made through the internal V.90 modem or 10/100 mbps Ethernet port, or via external devices, such as a CDPD (cellular) modem.
